title: Sabbath Morning Class: Messengers Of The Nation

sense.text: We all have a job to do in the nation of Israel: to be messengers, promoting the Most High’s truth and getting the gospel out to the four corners of the earth. It starts here, because the Bible is chosen and selected for us, the Israelites. A lot of people think their local minister, their pastor, understands the scriptures. He does not. Christ tells us why he speaks the way he does: “Who hath ears to hear, let him hear”, who has understanding, let him understand.

The disciples, the apostles, ask Christ, “Why speakest thou unto them in parables?” Why don’t you speak plainly to the people so they all can understand? Christ answers, “Because it is given unto you to know the mysteries of the kingdom of heaven”. That is us: it is given to us to know the mysteries. “But to them it is not given.”
“For whosoever hath, to him shall be given, and he shall have more abundance: but whosoever hath not, from him shall be taken away even that he hath.”

“Therefore speak I to them in parables: because they seeing see not”. Our people see a Bible and don’t understand the scriptures. “And hearing they hear not, neither do they understand.”

When I was in the church I didn’t understand one word the Bible was saying. It was always confusing to me, and that’s why I would fall asleep in church all the time: one, because it was boring, two, because some of the time the sermon was in Creole or in French, and I don’t speak Creole, so I didn’t know what he was saying. My grandmother would pop me upside the head every time I fell asleep. Then I went over to the Catholic Church, and you already know the Catholic Church: that’s the demonic church, demonic music. A one-hour mass, boring. I would never tell my family church was boring, because you don’t say something like that. I believed in God, at least I thought, but I didn’t know how to tell my family I didn’t like going to church. So whenever all the cousins met at our grandmother’s house, I wanted to go with my other grandmother, because she never went to church and we didn’t have to wake up 6:00 a.m. My mother would call and say, ‘you think you slick’. That was true: church was boring. The sermons made no sense.

Now, coming to the truth, we understand it is because the Most High is not dealing with them. It’s a one-hour mass of pure vomit. One time a teacher of mine said, ‘you need Jesus’, and invited me to her church, a huge church. It was different: the music went boom boom boom, huge flat screens all over the place, they even had an ATM machine. I was like, damn, these guys can go. But it was the same thing; the only difference was the music. Still no understanding. Here in the nation of Israel we are giving our people the understanding of the scriptures. That’s what makes the Israelites so dangerous: we know what we’re talking about.

“And in them is fulfilled the prophecy of Esaias”. Isaiah prophesied about our people: “By hearing ye shall hear, and shall not understand”. We hear the Bible, we hear the words of God, whether we are Lutheran, Catholic, Pentecostal, Episcopalian, Baptist or non-denominational, but we don’t understand. “And seeing ye shall see, and shall not perceive”: they see it and don’t perceive what the writings are saying.

“For this people’s heart is waxed gross”: this people’s mind, because the heart is the mind. “And their ears are dull of hearing”, dull of hearing, “and their eyes they have closed; lest at any time they should see with their eyes, and hear with their ears, and should understand with their heart, and should be converted, and I should heal them.”

See what the Most High is saying: I made the people’s minds like that. Why? Lest they should be converted. The Most High appointed our people not to understand the Bible, and only a small remnant will understand.

All of us can relate to this scripture, because most of us came out of the church, some more diligent than others. “Stay yourselves”: stay yourselves where? In the scriptures, in the Bible. “And wonder”: a brother in the back said it means to meditate on the scriptures, on the law, statutes, commandments and precepts. Meditating, studying, analyzing, yes; and the Bible’s own word for it is study. When you are wondering you are curious, you want to search, and all of that is studying.

“Cry ye out, and cry”: that is talking about teaching. “They are drunken, but not with wine”: our people are drunken with lies, with philosophies, with Christianity. Christianity has over 40 different denominations with the same book. That’s why some of our brothers say, ‘I’m not gonna join the Christian church’: it makes no sense, it’s confusion, it’s chaos.

“They stagger, but not with strong drink”: it’s mental. We are staggering in lies through the educational system, through the religious system and through the political system, because those are the three main areas where people say, this is where you’re gonna learn who you are. You’re gonna be an upright, standing citizen through religion, through your belief in God as a Caucasian man; through education; and through politics, this is the political party you should join that will help you become better Americans. It’s all lies.

“For the Lord hath poured out upon you the spirit of deep sleep”: our people out there are asleep. God says he “hath closed your eyes: the prophets and your rulers, the seers hath he covered.” These are the ministers, the pastors. Their eyes are covered as well as our people’s.

“And the vision of all is become unto you as the words of a book that is sealed”: the Bible. The words of the book are sealed. “Which men deliver to one that is learned”. Why does it say learned? Because he has a license: Esau has given him paperwork that says you are an officially ordained minister. “Saying, Read this, I pray thee”: give me the understanding of my identity in the Bible. “And he saith, I cannot; for it is sealed”.

These ministers don’t literally say, I cannot give you the understanding; they are too prideful. But their answer will let you understand he doesn’t know what he is talking about. That’s why a lot of our people left the church. They went to the minister for answers and said, listen, something’s not right. ‘Don’t worry, God is for us, God loves us.’ Minister, I’m not talking about love, I’m saying we are being oppressed, our people. ‘Brother, all races are good in Jesus.’ No, minister. ‘Brother, you asking too many questions, show up on Sunday for church.’ They don’t like that.

“And the book is delivered to him that is not learned, saying, Read this, I pray thee: and he saith, I am not learned.” This is the one who believes he was called to be a minister. He is not licensed, but he has been able to establish a church.

precepts.why:
This is it right here. Stay yourselves in the Bible, and the wondering is this: “Study to shew thyself approved unto God”. The wonder is study. Stay yourselves in the Bible and study. When you’re wondering, yes, you’re meditating, you’re studying, you’re analyzing.

But remember, brothers, as upcoming teachers we want to use the words of our Bible when we give our people the understanding, showing them what it says in the Old Testament and what it says in the New Testament. Paul said study; Isaiah said wonder. When you’re wondering you’re curious, you want to search, and all of that is studying. That’s why we study.

Why do we study? “The heart of the righteous studieth to answer”: the mind of the righteous studies to answer. That’s why we have the Bible open every day, why we’re watching the videos, listening to the scriptures, listening to the classes: because we want answers, and the Bible has those answers. “But the mouth of the wicked poureth out evil things.”

sense.text:
These messengers we have been reading about are not messengers sent by the Most High. Think about all of us in this room. One officer was trying to be a minister in the world, in Ghana. But most of us in the world weren’t trying to be ministers; we were going about our daily lives. Some brothers were trying to be Iceberg Slim, some were trying to own multiple companies, nothing wrong with that, some were trying to go to the NBA, some wanted to be football players. Hell, some of us didn’t have nothing; some said, I don’t even expect to make it to 30 years old. Completely lost. None of us said we’re gonna be teachers of the Bible. That’s how you know this is of God: none of us knew each other, and the only reason we know each other is the Bible. It’s the words of God that brought us together.

“I have not sent these prophets”, God says through Jeremiah, “yet they ran”. They ran to become a licensed minister, an ordained minister, because of Esau. The heavenly Father did not send them, but they will convince society that they are ordained ministers sent by God. You’re gonna find a group of teachers, a group of prophets, whom God did not send, and you have to make the difference: is this minister teaching of God, or is he a false minister?

One clue: the Bible says Jesus Christ is a black man with white woolly hair, and millions of our people don’t even know that. A lot of our people you meet will say, ‘brother, color doesn’t matter.’ Brothers, realize we are at war, at war to win the minds of our people. God says he never sent these teachers who teach a Caucasian image of Jesus, who teach that God loves all races. Even though they became licensed, became ordained ministers, even with a congregation of twenty thousand, God says, I didn’t send them.

“I have not spoken to them, yet they prophesied”: God has not spoken to them, but they decided to teach with the Bible.

precepts.why:
Here is why they choose to go into that field, why they decide to be ministers and teachers. “The heads thereof judge for reward”: these are our political leaders and our religious leaders. They judge the people for reward; they’re looking for money. “And the priests thereof teach for hire, and the prophets thereof divine for money”.

This is why people do it: covetousness. Remember the rapper who started to be a preacher? What the hell. He went from rapping to preaching. Remember in Dead Presidents, after the robbery, one of them decided to be a preacher, a minister, and the others laughed at him for thinking he was good because he was a minister. Anybody just decides to be a minister. That’s what they are showing you: they ran, but God did not send them.

sense.text:
Here is what Isaiah says about these leaders, the messengers that society says are messengers of God, leaders of God. We are showing you they are not. We are the messengers of God.

“Because ye have said, We have made a covenant with death, and with hell are we at agreement”. Our people have made a covenant and agreement with death, meaning with sin, and with hell, and hell represents captivity. We have made a covenant with death and with captivity: we are in agreement to be captive here in Babylon, in agreement to be on the bottom of all races.

“When the overflowing scourge shall pass through, it shall not come unto us”: we’re not gonna get jacked up. That’s what Israel believes. But every time, and we’ll prove it, from 1865 with the Emancipation to the Jim Crow era to the civil rights movement to 2020, it’s the same song: why are we oppressed? When will we become free? When will we be equal to other races? “For we have made lies our refuge”: our people have made lies their refuge, “and under falsehood have we hid ourselves”.

precepts.why:
Remember, when you read the books of prophecy, they cover many different time periods. Isaiah was talking about his own time, about the time of Babylon, the time of Persia, the time of the Greeks, the time of Rome, and he is talking about America.

“Wherefore thus saith the Holy One of Israel, Because ye despise this word”: Blacks and Latinos despise this word, the word of the Lord, his law. “And trust in oppression”: they trust in politics, they trust in religion. “And perverseness, and stay thereon”. The same people who made lies their refuge trust in oppression and stay on it.

sense.text:
A quick little history. Remember, very few people are selected and chosen for the Most High’s mission. Christianity has over 400 million followers; everybody and their momma is a Christian. You have MS-13 Christians chopping off heads, selling drugs, killing people in the name of Jesus, kidnapping, extortion, prostitution. Everybody says, ‘I’m a Christian’. But just because you have all those numbers, all those followers, doesn’t mean there is any truth to it.

“Now Jehoshaphat had riches and honour in abundance”: Jehoshaphat was one of the kings of Judah. “And joined affinity with Ahab”: Ahab was one of the kings of the Northern Kingdom. The Northern Kingdom are the Latino tribes, the Hispanic tribes; Judah is the American Negroes. That’s our identity in the Bible, and now we’re reading the history of what happened.

“And after certain years he went down to Ahab to Samaria. And Ahab killed sheep and oxen for him in abundance”, and “persuaded him to go up with him to Ramoth–gilead.” Ahab, king of the Northern Kingdom, was wicked as hell, and he wants Jehoshaphat, king of Judah, who stood with the Lord and was all about the laws and the commandments for the people, to come and join with him. “Wilt thou go with me to Ramoth–gilead? And he answered him, I am as thou art, and my people as thy people”. Remember, by this time the Northern Kingdom had already split; there was already a division.

“And Jehoshaphat said unto the king of Israel, Enquire, I pray thee, at the word of the Lord to day.” Before we go to war together, enquire of the Lord. You see who Jehoshaphat’s counsellor was: let’s go to the Lord first.

“Therefore the king of Israel gathered together of prophets four hundred men”. Four hundred prophets. The kings are sitting on their thrones together, and each prophet comes up and prophesies victory: King Ahab, you shall prosper, you will succeed in your battle. “Shall we go to Ramoth–gilead to battle, or shall I forbear?” Should we stop and not go to this war because we’re gonna lose? “And they said, Go up; for God will deliver it into the king’s hand.” Four hundred men prophesied victory for King Ahab.

“But Jehoshaphat said, Is there not here a prophet of the Lord besides, that we might enquire of him?” Hold on, hold on. Those are four hundred prophets that said we’re gonna win, but something’s not right here. Is there anybody left besides these four hundred that we can ask?

The kings are set up as kings, but they are not prophets; they go to the prophets. They are kings over the people to have power, they control the army, they control resources, but they are not prophets. There is a difference. King Hezekiah was a king but he was not a prophet; David was a king and a prophet. There is a difference between being a king and being called to be a prophet.

“There is yet one man, by whom we may enquire of the Lord: but I hate him”. Why does he say that? “For he never prophesied good unto me, but always evil”: he never got nothing good to say about me. “The same is Micaiah the son of Imla. And Jehoshaphat said, Let not the king say so.” Wait, Ahab, don’t talk like that; let’s find out, maybe he’s gonna say something good. Four hundred men said y’all are gonna win the war, go forth to battle; why did Jehoshaphat still want to find out if anybody was left? He saw something in the spirit with those men.

“Fetch quickly Micaiah the son of Imla.” Each king is sitting on his throne, “clothed in their robes”, “at the entering in of the gate of Samaria; and all the prophets prophesied before them.” Zedekiah “had made him horns of iron, and said, Thus saith the Lord, With these thou shalt push Syria until they be consumed.” “And all the prophets prophesied so, saying, Go up to Ramoth–gilead, and prosper”.

“And the messenger that went to call Micaiah spake to him, saying, Behold, the words of the prophets declare good to the king with one assent”: all in unison, all in one accord, saying good things to the king. “Let thy word therefore, I pray thee, be like one of theirs, and speak thou good.” “And Micaiah said, As the Lord liveth, even what my God saith, that will I speak.” I’m only gonna say what the Lord shows to me. That’s how I’m rolling.

Micaiah comes up and everybody’s looking; remember, Ahab told Jehoshaphat he never says anything good. “Micaiah, shall we go to Ramoth–gilead to battle, or shall I forbear? And he said, Go ye up, and prosper, and they shall be delivered into your hand.” “And the king said to him, How many times shall I adjure thee that thou say nothing but the truth to me in the name of the Lord?” Tell me the truth: what did you see in the vision? Be honest.

“Then he said, I did see all Israel scattered upon the mountains, as sheep that have no shepherd”. Damn, Micaiah just went against 400 prophets. Micaiah didn’t give a damn; he said the truth. Numbers don’t mean nothing: you stand by the Bible. “And the Lord said, These have no master; let them return therefore every man to his house in peace.”

“Did I not tell thee that he would not prophesy good unto me, but evil?” I told you, every time. That’s why he put him in jail. So you had 400 men saying you’re gonna win the war, and only one was telling the truth and spoke the true vision: no, you’re not gonna win, you’re gonna lose. And when you read on, the Lord put a spirit on all those men to prophesy that to the king; that’s what Micaiah was showing him. Then they smacked him in the face and asked which way the Lord went from them to speak to him.

Think about it: all these men saying they’re gonna win the war, and here is Micaiah alone. But Micaiah wasn’t scared. He told the total truth: you’re gonna lose, I don’t care what 400 men said to you, the Lord is going to have you lose. He wasn’t afraid, and that’s how we got to be. Christ said don’t be ashamed to speak of me; if you’re ashamed of me, I’m gonna be ashamed of you before the Father. We don’t want to be that bunch. We want to always stand for the Most High and Christ and his laws. The world has never seen black and Latino men and sisters standing firm for the Bible.

We have been reading about all those false ministers, false prophets, false leaders, false messengers. Paul says, “For such are false apostles, deceitful workers, transforming themselves into the apostles of Christ.”
“And no marvel”: don’t be shocked, “for Satan himself is transformed into an angel of light.”

“Therefore it is no great thing”: it’s not shocking, “if his ministers also be transformed as the ministers of righteousness”. They appear to be ministers, teachers of righteousness. “Whose end shall be according to their works”: the judgment is death. That’s the judgment.

These ministers and leaders we read about want to support Babylon. Now we’re about to read about men that are against Babylon.

“For a small moment have I forsaken thee”. Remember, the Northern Kingdom was conquered starting in 1492; the Southern Kingdom in the 1600s, some even in the fifteen hundreds, but the bulk in the 1600s. 1619, 1700, 1800: that’s over 200 years, two centuries, and God says that was just a small moment.

“But with great mercies will I gather thee.” How is God gonna gather us? He’s gonna use teachers to teach his word.

precepts.why:
For a small moment God forsook us. What did he do? He sent the white man against us during the 1600s. Let’s see what type of men they were. “They shall come all for violence”: who? The Chaldeans, the Babylonians. When you read the scriptures, God caused the white man, the daughter of Babylon, to come against us. The white man is the daughter of Babylon: Esau, Edom.

“Their faces shall sup up as the east wind”: when they came, where did they come from? From the eastern hemisphere over to the west. “And they shall gather the captivity as the sand”: they gathered our people as the sand and led us into captivity.

“And they shall scoff at the kings”: they scoffed at the kings over here in West Africa, they scoffed at the kings in the Congo, they scoffed at the kings over in America, which was the Northern Kingdom as well. “And the princes shall be a scorn unto them: they shall deride every strong hold; for they shall heap dust, and take it.” The dust represents confusion. Our people have accepted confusion about their race, confusion about what to support, confusion about their own God.

“Then shall his mind change”: this man who would lead our people captive, his mind would change. Look at slavery in the United States: Esau’s mind changed. Remember the 1600s and 1700s: ruthless. The brothers have read the slave narratives, listened to them, seen the pictures of how brutal this man was, and in school they don’t cover all of it. In high school it was a one-week lesson, 40 minutes each day, Monday through Friday, the most watered-down history of slavery I’ve ever heard, and the one teaching it was uncomfortable: some of these men weren’t the best men, but you had good slave masters, merciful slave masters.

The timeline runs from the Atlantic slave trade and slavery in the colonial United States through the Revolutionary War, the antebellum period, the Civil War and Reconstruction, to the Jim Crow era and the civil rights movement. The Jim Crow era is post-slavery, post-1865, so it changed: all right, we’re not gonna have chains on you, we’re not gonna be selling you. But what happened then? The KKK, lynchings, the Jim Crow era. We are still in captivity. Remember, in Exodus they said, ‘let us deal wisely with them.’ That’s why Habakkuk says his mind shall change: slavery just took a change. The type of slavery changed; we were still in slavery, it is just different now.

sense.text:
Dr. Joy DeGruy says African people and people of African descent are extremely resilient, ‘matter of fact I think we’re a miracle.’ This is all of the Most High. We got to give credit to the Most High; he’s been merciful unto us.

“It is of the Lord’s mercies that we are not consumed”, “because his compassions fail not.” That’s what it is: the Most High has been merciful to blacks and Hispanics.

The Moynihan report, a document written in 1965, says it too, in its most controversial chapter, ‘the tangle of pathology’: ‘that the Negro American has survived at all is extraordinary; a lesser people might have simply died out, as indeed others have.’ The fact that we’ve even survived what the Most High put us through is amazing. It shows how resilient black people are, and it is of the Lord’s mercies.

“And among these nations shalt thou find no ease, neither shall the sole of thy foot have rest”. This goes into what we read where it said Reconstruction era and Jim Crow era. Among these nations we would find no ease. It only changed; we were still captive. They said, okay, we’re gonna take the chains off, but we’re gonna hunt you down, we’re gonna change the laws.

“But the Lord shall give thee there a trembling heart, and failing of eyes”. Trembling of heart, because you don’t know if you’re gonna survive.

Melba Pattillo, one of the Little Rock Nine, wrote the book Warriors Don’t Cry. As a little girl she remembered firebombings, where you don’t know if a white man’s gonna drive down and bomb the whole house. She lived through that. These sisters was no joke: they were doing all that for Judah to have rights; the Most High was moving in spirit, using many different figures. And then in the end of the book, after all that happened, she married Esau.

There’s so many records and details on what happened in slavery, how ruthless Esau is. That’s why the Most High said he would send ‘the worst of the heathen’.

“What thing shall I take to witness for thee? what thing shall I liken to thee, O daughter of Jerusalem? what shall I equal to thee, that I may comfort thee, O virgin daughter of Zion? for thy breach is great like the sea: who can heal thee?” After all the way he’s oppressed us, the Most High says, how can I equal it.

This goes to show you our oppression has been the worst. There’s no oppression like blacks and Latinos. When you have conversations with people they’ll say, well, everybody was oppressed. But ours was the worst by far. What you will have is racist Moabites, Chinese, Japanese, Caucasians that try to say, let’s show that everybody’s been oppressed, let’s try to water it down. No: our oppression has been the worst. That’s why God says, what shall I equal to thee, that I may comfort thee.

“Come, and let us return unto the Lord: for he hath torn, and he will heal us”. He hath torn, but will heal us. In the healing process he used many different figures to start to heal us, and here is an example: Denmark Vesey, from the book Before the Mayflower by Lerone Bennett Jr. Vesey tried to have a successful slave insurrection, but it was told to the slave masters and they hung him. Look at where his frame of mind was during that time for his people.

Vesey won a lottery and purchased his freedom. He worked as a carpenter in Charleston, South Carolina, accumulated money and property, and was respected by Negroes and whites; by his own admission he was satisfied with his own condition. Yet he risked everything in a bold effort to free other men. He had the chance to go to Liberia, to Africa, and he decided to stay; he wanted to stay and see what he could do for his fellow creatures. Denmark Vesey was from St. Thomas, and they brought him to America; he was some twenty years the slave of a slave trader, traveled widely, learned several languages, and learned that slavery was evil. He had a deep and unquenchable hatred of slavery and slaveholders, and reached a point where he could not bear to have a white person in his presence.

For four or five years he played the role of an agitator. Men, he saw, must not only be dissatisfied; they must be so dissatisfied they will act. You can’t just be upset; you have to be so angry you will commit action. What is the action that we’re doing? Organizing, teaching. But we can’t be like our people: you get mad and you burn down a neighborhood. No, no. We get mad, but we organize.

He told the slaves their lives were so miserable that even death would be an improvement. He read to them from the Bible how the children of Israel were delivered out of Egypt from bondage, but warned that God helps those who help themselves, and always the words of Joshua were on his lips. If he saw slaves with the white men in the street he would rebuke them, and when they replied, but we are slaves, he would say with biting sarcasm, you deserve to be slaves. This brother was cold. He was from St. Thomas, so you know what tribe that is. Asked what can we do, he would tell the story of Hercules and the wagoner whose wagon was stuck at the bottom of the hill: the wagoner began to cry and pray, and Hercules told him to put the whip to the team. Always, everywhere, Denmark Vesey was teaching. He said, we are free, but the white people here won’t let us be so, and the only way is to raise up and fight the whites. Vesey was all about helping his people.

He employed every stratagem to induce them to join him. It wasn’t a one-time thing; it was constant, persistent effort. Vesey was free, and he would remain with slaves and teach slaves, reading them every passage in the newspapers that related to St. Domingo, Haiti, and every pamphlet he could lay his hands on that had any connection with slavery. Ridiculing, taunting, threatening, he gained a hold on the minds of the Negroes in Charleston; many slaves feared him more than they feared their masters, and one man said he feared Vesey more than he feared God. He didn’t play.

Then Vesey switched from the role of agitator to the role of organizer. Around Christmas of 1821 he chose lieutenants and perfected his organization. This isn’t a one-man job when it comes to waking our people up; it is collective effort. He enlisted slave artisans and class leaders in the Methodist church. He had Gullah Jack, an African-born sorcerer who practiced voodoo, and blind Philip, who reportedly could see ghosts: timid recruits were carried to his house, and blind Philip would ask them why they looked so timorous and quote Holy Scripture, ‘let not your heart be troubled’. The chief lieutenant was Peter, a first-rate ship carpenter with an organizing ability bordering on genius; ice water ran in his veins. He volunteered for the most difficult assignment, the surprise and capture of the main guardhouse.

Peter was in charge of organization; he decided who should be approached and who shouldn’t. He pinpointed the greatest danger to a slave revolt, the house servants: don’t mention it to those waiting men who receive presents of old coats from their masters, or they’ll betray us. So Peter said, you let me deal with the Coons. Vesey and Peter perfected a cell-like organization: only the leaders knew the details, and the average recruit knew nothing except the name of his leader, so a single recruit arrested could not endanger the whole plot. Whole plantations signed up and weapons were constructed. It has been estimated that some nine thousand slaves were recruited. The reason Vesey wasn’t able to carry out his mission is because too many people knew about it, and eventually brothers sold out.

precepts.why: Vesey could have went to Africa, but he stayed. It shows you his character: just like Moses. “By faith Moses, when he was come to years, refused to be called the son of Pharaoh’s daughter; Choosing rather to suffer affliction with the people of God, than to enjoy the pleasures of sin for a season”. And look at that, brothers: “for a season”. It’s only gonna last for a season.

“Then shall the righteous man stand in great boldness before the face of such as have afflicted him”. That’s how they describe Denmark Vesey. When you read this book it describes Nat Turner, it describes Gabriel Prosser: these men stood up in great boldness. That was during their time, the 1800s, and the Most High was using them.

Go a couple years ahead, to Marcus Garvey. Jamaica rejected him; he went to Panama, and everywhere he traveled the Negro was always at the bottom. When he came to America, Judah accepted Garvey’s teachings and gave him support: a significant following of ordinary working people, over one million followers in the 1920s and 30s. Before 1865 Denmark Vesey was recruiting slaves, persistent, setting up men under him that had different talents; almost a hundred years later Garvey was recruiting, recruiting, recruiting, because they saw the same thing Denmark saw, the same thing Gabriel Prosser saw, the same thing Nat Turner saw: you have to liberate your people.

Malcolm X’s parents, Earl and Louise Little, were the typical Garvey family. Wherever they went they started chapters; they were always mobile, but always teaching, recruiting people to join the movement. And mind you, they didn’t even have the truth, but they understood how our people are oppressed, at the bottom. Louise Little was the secretary of the Lansing UNIA and wrote the reports of meetings; Garvey set up the Black Cross Nurses, women who went to the homes of Garvey families to make sure they were healthy and getting enough food. These sisters was getting down. There’s always stuff to do for the woman. All you got to do is get in where you fit in: you know your talents, you know how you can assist. Everybody don’t have the same talent, everybody don’t have the same gift. That sister didn’t have the truth, but she understood to assist and support black men. They were not leaders, not heads of the organization, but they were local and they were committed. That’s the point: that you are committed.

Gil Noble says his parents taught him not to confront racism but to get around it, to accommodate, because they didn’t want him to get killed or join one of these groups. That’s the same way I grew up; I rarely heard racism dealt with. Some of your parents raised you to be timid, to assimilate; some raised you to be an agitator. We’re all coming with different personalities, different spirits, but the Most High is calling us to this truth. Garvey was in the streets of Harlem, teaching on the street about pride, standing up for your race. It’s the same thing we’re doing now. The only difference, brothers: this movement is God’s movement. All the movements before were movements of men. They did whatever they could for their people, being used by the Most High, but it was not the Most High’s movement, because they only understood so much. You got to have respect: with the little that they knew, Nat Turner and Denmark Vesey still did a lot for their people.

sense.text:
We read earlier about the messengers, the ministers and preachers who don’t know the Bible; then we got into the history of racism and how Esau destroyed us, and what happened in Denmark Vesey’s time and Marcus Garvey’s time. Now we’re dealing with this time period right here.

“Behold, I will send you Elijah the prophet before the coming of the great and dreadful day of the Lord”. This was a prophecy that Elijah would come back and teach. The fact that we know who we are, based off of Deuteronomy 28, proves Elijah has come.

precepts.why: “For I think that God hath set forth us the apostles last, as it were appointed to death: for we are made a spectacle unto the world, and to angels, and to men.” God has set forth us the apostles last. You saved the best for last: we have been appointed to bring his truth out last. All these movements have come and gone; this last one is God’s movement.

sense.text:
Notice it says he hath set forth us the apostles last. “So the last shall be first, and the first last: for many be called, but few chosen.” Why does he say the last shall be first? This could be used on different levels, and there are a couple of understandings you can use that scripture on, but this is the literal understanding during the time Christ said it.

The first shall be last and the last first: it’s talking about the first, and the prophets that came later. That’s the correct understanding. At that time the scribes, Pharisees and chief priests were committed the job to teach and guide Israel. They were first; that was their job. They were chosen first, and they were not doing it; they were more focused on position and power. What did they do? They rejected the Messiah.

That’s why, when you see Jesus Christ going to recruit Peter, James, the apostles, they say, Christ, I’m not worthy, I’m not worthy, because they’re last; they don’t look at themselves like that. None of us here was trying to be a teacher, trying to be a preacher. We were going about our ordinary lives: some of y’all were Christians, some of y’all were Muslims, some of you Five Percent, somebody was on the street corners hustling. In your mind you did not say I’m gonna be an Israelite, I’m gonna teach. You did not know that was your calling.

So the last shall be first, and the first last: “for many be called, but few chosen.”

precepts.why: Remember what Christ said: the last shall be first and the first last. “The Son of man must suffer many things, and be rejected of the elders and chief priests and scribes, and be slain, and be raised the third day.” The elders, chief priests and scribes: these are the first, and they rejected him.

The first shall be last and the last first. “Then spake Jesus to the multitude, and to his disciples, Saying, The scribes and the Pharisees sit in Moses’ seat”. They sat in Moses’ seat: they were the first, the ones whose job it was to teach and guide Israel.

Hitting the same scriptures, going in a circle: “I think that God hath set forth us the apostles last”. The apostles were the last, and God set them forth to bring his truth out. Matthew 20:16, Luke 9:22, Matthew 23:1 and 1 Corinthians 4:9 are the foundation: the scribes, chief priests and elders that sat in Moses’ seat were first, and the apostles set forth last.

We’re addressing the first: the scribes, the Pharisees, the chief priests. “Then gathered the chief priests and the Pharisees a council, and said, What do we? for this man doeth many miracles.” Who’s this man? Jesus Christ. His teachings were true, it had power, and the people were believing Christ. “If we let him thus alone, all men will believe on him: and the Romans shall come and take away both our place and nation.” There you go: these are the first, focused on their place and their position.

Why do you think Christ said the scribes and Pharisees sit in Moses’ seat? “Now about the midst of the feast Jesus went up into the temple, and taught. And the Jews marvelled, saying, How knoweth this man letters, having never learned?” The Jews that marveled were the first, the leaders. How does this man know the letters of Moses, having never learned from their schools? Christ never went to any of their schools, but he had more understanding than they did.

sense.text:
“And this gospel”: this good news. The good news that blacks, Hispanics, the descendants of the slave trade, our people in West Africa, East Africa and Iraq, all our people that have suffered oppression from Deuteronomy chapter 28, and their children, are going to be saved. This gospel is that Christ is a black man with white woolly hair and he’s only coming to save our race back. That’s the good news.

“Shall be preached in all the world for a witness unto all nations”: why unto all nations? Because we are scattered in all nations. “And then shall the end come”: when this gospel reaches the whole world, that’s when the end is going to come, because the 144,000, these select men, are scattered, and we’re trying to find them.

There are many different forms of outreach. Camp: a lot of times people call because they see the brothers in the camp videos. Camp is the most dangerous form of outreach, the most dangerous form of recruiting, because we could get stabbed, shot, anything could happen; it’s face-to-face contact and we don’t know what’s going to happen. Fly missions are dangerous too, because once again it’s face to face; we’re not behind a computer screen, we’re up front, close encounters.

Social media is a form of outreach: sharing the videos on Twitter, Facebook, Instagram. That’s keeping your day busy rather than just searching. Whenever the captains’ offices share the videos in your congregation, all the sisters, the kids, everybody with a social media platform, the first thing they should do is share it, share it, share it.

Personal encounters: going to the store, going about your day, you meet somebody, and a lot of our people talk, ‘I’ve been wanting to join y’all.’ That’s where you’ve got the business cards: professional, it looks clean, it’s nice and precise, and it shows what we represent. What you don’t want to do: back on the plantation, working at Sears, I bumped into the mother from The Cosby Show. I ain’t give a damn, I said she’s getting this info. I printed out a Sears receipt, ripped it off, wrote the website on it, and while she was shopping I said, ‘Excuse me miss, I’m sorry to disturb your day, I really need you to see this information, this can save our people.’ She said, ‘Thank you young man.’ Who knows if she read it. That was the best I could do at that time, but that’s not the way to represent Israel United in Christ. Now we can be prepared: carry the flyers, carry the business cards, because there are thousands of us, and you don’t know who you’re going to meet; you’re already ready to recruit.

And at the very bottom of outreach, you’ve got some people that are with us that don’t mention us at all. They don’t do nothing, they don’t say nothing; they’re behind the scenes watching online, and they just never mention the truth to nobody.

precepts.why:
This is about outreach, about us teaching, about us recruiting, and it is very important. If we’re serious about going home, we would be recruiting, constantly teaching, constantly putting the truth out there. That is our duty.

“A man that hath travelled knoweth many things; and he that hath much experience will declare wisdom.” Then verse 10: “He that hath no experience knoweth little: but he that hath travelled is full of prudence.” That’s why we always say support the brothers traveling to different countries, different areas. When we went to Ghana it was a complete, total different experience: we handed out over 3,000 flyers and not one of them touched the ground.

Over there you had an unbeliever, the police chief, who doesn’t believe in the truth, but he said, ‘I’m going to make sure your brothers are protected; nobody’s going to touch y’all.’ That’s why the scripture says be wise as a serpent, harmless as a dove. Even though some of our people don’t believe, you’ve got to know how to use them; if you know how to deal with them, they’ll help you get this truth out. They will be an asset to help us get this gospel further, to the eastern hemisphere, further into Iraq. There are still countries we have not touched yet.

Read it again: the man that hath much experience will declare wisdom, because Judah here in New York is different from Judah in Indiana. In New York you try to get flyers to Judah and Judah walks past you; they don’t give a damn. The brothers in Indiana are ready. Camp there was like three people walking every 30 minutes, mostly cars, so the brothers in the other states don’t even have a lot of foot traffic, and they’re still going strong teaching. When we did camp in Indiana I was telling cars to pull over, and Judah actually pulled over the car and got out. It’s different.

So seeing the world, brothers, travel. You probably was traveling bringing drugs for cartels, I don’t know what the hell you was doing, but now you’re traveling to bring God’s truth out. That’s a reason to visit Indiana, Tennessee, Arizona, Mississippi, Alabama, Oregon. There’s a lot of ground we did not cover. Recruiting never stops. As we travel we learn different spirits, we see different things, and y’all learn from the different congregations. That’s why it’s good to travel.

Visiting different locations, there’s no camp like New York. New York is a battle ground, Chicago too. At camp in New York you’ve got the LGBT right there, the Bloods, the Latin Kings, the Five Percent Nation, Muslims, so many different beliefs, while another state may be predominantly Muslims and a couple LGBT. There are so many different spirits in New York at the same time, with two thousand people walking past you every couple minutes. It’s not saying it’s the best, but it is serious when we’re here in New York teaching.

“For we stretch not ourselves beyond our measure, as though we reached not unto you: for we are come as far as to you also in preaching the gospel of Christ”. Then verse 15: “Not boasting of things without our measure, that is, of other men’s labours; but having hope, when your faith is increased, that we shall be enlarged by you according to our rule abundantly”. Now watch verse 16: “To preach the gospel in the regions beyond you”. That’s the work: carrying the gospel out to the regions beyond, “and not to boast in another man’s line of things made ready to our hand.”

That’s what this is about. That’s why we must always be ready to preach this truth, always be ready to recruit. Garvey, without internet technology, was able to get over 1 million people to join this movement. Israel United in Christ never stops; we have to keep pushing this gospel. The work don’t stop. It’s an honor for the brothers to be at camp, but there are different ways to push the truth. Not everybody goes to camp, but that don’t mean you can’t help assist in recruiting, in getting our brothers and sisters to join.

“Their line is gone out through all the earth”: their line means their teaching is going out to all the world. “And their words to the end of the world”: God is saying that his word is going to go forth to the ends of the world.

“What shall one then answer the messengers of the nation?” It is an honor to be at camp, an honor to be on fly missions: we are God’s messengers. “That the Lord hath founded Zion, and the poor of his people shall trust in it.”

That’s why, with still many neighborhoods and communities that have not heard this message, we’ve got to be traveling throughout the area, throughout the city. And to those saying, ‘Dang, I’m not at camp’: that’s why there’s outreach, there’s social media postings, sharing, supporting. Support, support, support. And you online: you’re taking too long, you need to join Israel United in Christ, because we’re serious about this. We are going to the eastern hemisphere.

All praises to the Most High, we’ve been able to establish congregations throughout Africa, but there are still places, Australia, the Philippines, all these islands with black people we’ve never met. Like that movie on Netflix where he meets the daughter he had in Vietnam that he never met: a lot of Judah was having sex with Vietnamese women, having kids, and Korean women, because blacks were in the Korean War. Our people are all over.

“I have set watchmen upon thy walls, O Jerusalem, which shall never hold their peace day nor night: ye that make mention of the Lord, keep not silence”: meaning you don’t stop, you continue to preach this message. “And give him no rest”: we can’t give the Most High no rest, “till he establish, and till he make Jerusalem a praise in the earth.” That’s what we’re waiting for: the new Jerusalem. The world don’t know about that. The Bible says Esau is the end of the world.

“The Lord hath sworn by his right hand, and by the arm of his strength, Surely I will no more give thy corn to be meat for thine enemies; and the sons of the stranger shall not drink thy wine, for the which thou hast laboured: But they that have gathered it shall eat it, and praise the Lord”.

Look at verse 10: “Go through, go through the gates; prepare ye the way of the people; cast up, cast up the highway; gather out the stones; lift up a standard for the people”: a banner for the people, let them know. “Behold, the Lord hath proclaimed unto the end of the world, Say ye to the daughter of Zion, Behold, thy salvation cometh”. That’s what we’re declaring: we’re telling our people, blacks and Hispanics, that they will be saved. “Behold, his reward is with him, and his work before him.”

sense.text:
Look what Paul says when he describes the nation of Israel. “And God hath set some in the church, first apostles”: the apostles had a very high calling; Christ went to them first. Peter, James, John, all these men were top, top leaders.

“Secondarily prophets”: Paul is showing us that some of our brothers will have that spirit of prophecy, to teach, to be able to see and understand visions, but they may not be on the level of the apostles, that responsibility. They’re not on that level, but they still play a part. “Thirdly teachers”: these teachers don’t have the understanding of prophecy; the Most High is not dealing with them on prophecy, and they’re not on the level of the apostles, but they can still teach, guide and organize.

“After that miracles, then gifts of healings”: during that time they were able to physically heal people. During this time some brothers can heal you through God’s word: counsellors, who can heal your spirit. Sometimes during the week your spirit is jacked up, and you need that one conversation with that brother. But in order for your spirit to get uplifted you have to be communicating. Some brothers are quiet and secretive, and that’s how Satan eats you up; the sisters too. There’s all kind of sin up in there, but they don’t want to say nothing, they don’t want to talk to nobody. You want to be mindful who you choose as a counselor, but don’t say nothing at all? We’re in here because we ain’t right, so you’ve got to talk. We can’t physically heal you of any sickness; you can change your diet and exercise, and we can counsel you with what the Bible says to heal your spirit.

“Helps”: these brothers and sisters may not be in the MOV, probably can’t go to camp, too old, too weak, whatever it is, but they can still help, still assist, whether financially, helping clean, donating, helping in the body, whatever ways they can. They still play a part. “Governments, diversities of tongues”: meaning different languages.

“Are all apostles? are all prophets?” Is everybody a prophet? No. The prophets are literally back, but everybody in here is not a prophet; the spirit of prophecy is not on everybody, and the Most High is not dealing with everybody on that level. That doesn’t mean you can’t learn and glean from who the Lord is dealing with on that level. “Are all teachers?” Not everybody is able to teach. “Are all workers of miracles? Have all the gifts of healing? do all speak with tongues? do all interpret?”

“But covet earnestly the best gifts: and yet shew I unto you a more excellent way.” When you keep reading on down, he goes into charity. Some brothers may not be able to physically help or be at all these different locations, but they have charity. They make that phone call to you when you’re sick; whenever you need, they’re always by your side. They will make it keeping the commandments, and Christ said one of the greatest commandments is to love your brother as you love yourself. Some brothers have that charity, some sisters have that charity: ‘Let me call and check up on you, let me make sure everything’s all right, let me see if you need help with anything.’ That’s charity: having that love and care for the body.

“Blessed is he that shall eat bread in the kingdom of God.” Now he is going to start the parable. “A certain man made a great supper, and bade many”: a certain man made a big supper and invited many to come.
“Come; for all things are now ready”: come, for all things are now ready for this dinner.

“And they all with one consent began to make excuse.” The Pharisees, the scribes, all of them are in here; that’s these religious leaders today, all making excuses for not doing the work. A piece of ground, five yoke of oxen, “I have married a wife, and therefore I cannot come.” Nobody wants to do the work.

“Then the master of the house being angry said to his servant, Go out quickly into the streets and lanes of the city, and bring in hither the poor, and the maimed, and the halt, and the blind”: bring these people to the supper. “And yet there is room”: there is still room left.

“Go out into the highways and hedges, and compel them to come in, that my house may be filled.” Compel our people. Brothers, sisters, that’s our job, and it starts first with the men. Every sanctuary has to be filled, and there’s never enough people, because once we fill up that house we get a new one. This is all a parable of going into the kingdom, but look at it also with these sanctuaries: we are going out and compelling our people to come in.

On the fly mission, giving out flyers, a brother says, ‘Nah, I’m good.’ We don’t accept no, unless you get that one demon that just straight up wants to fight, or some white people that just say no. A lot of our people are saying no just because they’re clueless: ‘Nah brother, I’m good.’ Nah brother, you ain’t good, come back over here. That’s how we have to deal, because whenever we give out these flyers our people are going to say no.

Compel them means we are not giving our people an option: you must come in. This is the truth without a shadow of a doubt; that’s what we’re showing our people. But you have to make your calling and election sure; that’s your job. So why are some brothers still confused? What are you to be confused about? Our people are being oppressed, and the Most High called you to help bring them in. ‘Is God dealing with me? I don’t know’: brother, get the hell out the way. The reason you’re in here is because the Most High called you, so what are you doubting for?

precepts.why:
Christ says from henceforth ye shall catch men. Peter was fishing. “Launch out into the deep, and let down your nets for a draught.” “Master, we have toiled all the night, and have taken nothing”: we’ve been trying to catch these fish all night and we can’t get nothing. “Nevertheless at thy word I will let down the net”: because you said it, Christ, I’ma do it, but we’ve been out all night and didn’t catch nothing.

“They inclosed a great multitude of fishes: and their net brake.” When they threw the net on the other side they had so much fish that the whole net broke. “And they beckoned unto their partners, which were in the other ship, that they should come and help them”: come, get over here quick. “And they came, and filled both the ships, so that they began to sink.”

“When Simon Peter saw it, he fell down at Jesus’ knees, saying, Depart from me; for I am a sinful man, O Lord.” This is Peter showing how humble he was. “For he was astonished”: he was shocked, and all that were with him, at the draught of the fishes; they’re saying, how did he know that? “And so was also James, and John, the sons of Zebedee, which were partners with Simon. And Jesus said unto Simon, Fear not; from henceforth thou shalt catch men.”

That’s what we’re doing when we’re trying to bring our people in: we’re going fishing. There are different kinds of bait you can use, different ways to catch fish. I don’t know how to physically fish, but when we’re out in the street we know how to catch souls; I know how to spiritually fish. Christ used the analogy of fishing for bringing our people into this walk. You have to know how to recruit. You cannot approach everybody the same; everybody is different, but you have to know how to deal with everybody. That’s why Paul said ‘I became all things unto all men, that I might by some means save some.’ That’s what this is about: saving our people.
One more scripture: “For it is written, I will destroy the wisdom of the wise, and will bring to nothing the understanding of the prudent.”

“For ye see your calling, brethren”: you have to see your calling. The reason you are in this room is because you are being called. Not everybody is chosen, but your works are going to show if you’re chosen, because if you believe, you’re going to take action. Look what we read about Denmark Vesey: a man has to be so angry, so displeased, that he will take action. So what are you doing to help our people join Israel United in Christ? This is an organization that sets a great example for our people to learn about Christ.

“How that not many wise men after the flesh, not many mighty”: some brothers that come in are financially well-off, powerful figures, but it’s rare; Paul says not many. “Not many noble”: basketball players. Some of them share the posts, but in their mind they’re thinking, ‘I don’t know if I could join them, I’m going to lose a lot of money, my contracts, my endorsements.’ That’s their trial. Some of them will forsake all, but some are going to follow behind the scenes. Al Sharpton, Louis Farrakhan, Cornel West: how are these figures not here, not chosen? What we could say is maybe in the future. Don’t hold your breath.

“But God hath chosen the foolish things of the world to confound the wise”: the foolish things of the world are us. “And God hath chosen the weak things of the world to confound the things which are mighty”. “And base things of the world, and things which are despised, hath God chosen”: you don’t get no lower than a black or Latino. “Yea, and things which are not, to bring to nought things that are”: that’s how the Most High says he’s going to bring this kingdom down.

So it is an honor to be called into this truth, but you’ve got to make your calling and election sure. Part of that is constantly communicating with the brothers, coming to the MOV program, going to the fundraisers: always being involved in the work.
